q: A stream in HoTT (a coinductive type) represents an infinite dynamical orbit because:
opts: A stream of A is defined by head: A and tail: Stream A, capturing the current state and the infinite future orbit corecursively
Streams are computable in finite time
exp: Coinductive streams: Stream(A) = {head: A, tail: Stream(A)}. A stream is an element a₀,a₁,a₂,… generated by unfolding f: B→A×B. The orbit of x₀ under dynamics f is the stream unfold(λx.(f(x),f(x)))(x₀). Bisimulation between streams is the coinductive version of topological conjugacy.
